free.a: Yes. All templates, AI features and PDF downloads are free. AI requests are limited per day to keep it that way for everyone.

ats.q: What is ATS and are the templates compatible?
ats.a: Applicant tracking systems read CVs before a human does. Our PDFs contain real text in a logical order. Templates marked ATS use a simple structure that parses best – use them for large companies and online portals.

data.a: Only in your browser (local storage). Nothing is uploaded unless you use an AI feature – then only the text needed for that request is sent and not stored.

ai.a: No – it is instructed to use only facts from your CV. Always read the suggestion before accepting it.

pages.q: What if my CV is longer than one page?
pages.a: Content flows to the next A4 page automatically. Each column continues on the next page, entries are never cut in half.

languages.q: Can I make the same CV in several languages?
languages.a: Yes. Use AI translation – it adapts job titles and wording to the target country. Export your CV first if you want to keep both versions.

final.title: Ready for your next job?
final.text: Create a professional CV now – it only takes a moment.

templates.subtitle: Each template has its own fixed layout (1, 2 or 3 columns) – you can still move sections between its columns. ATS-marked templates are the safest choice for online applications.

header.intro: Your name and contact details, so a recruiter can e-mail or call you. Add a photo if it is common in the target country.

experience.intro: Start with your most recent job. Describe results, not just duties – AI can help turn them into strong bullet points.
experience.lead: Now let's add your work experience.

education.intro: Your highest or most relevant degree first. Add courses or a thesis only if they matter for the job.
education.lead: Next, let's fill in your education.

skills.intro: List tools, technologies and soft skills that match the jobs you apply for. 6–12 skills work best.
skills.lead: Now it's time for your skills.

languages.intro: Use the CEFR scale (A1–C2) – recruiters across Europe understand it.

summary.intro: 2–4 sentences at the top of your CV: who you are, what you are best at and what you are looking for. Let AI write a first draft from your experience.

extra.intro: Projects, certificates and interests can make the difference. Everything is optional – empty sections are not printed.

finish.intro: Choose the template, arrange its sections, tailor the CV to a job offer with AI and download a PDF.

experience.title: Add your experience
experience.text: Most employers expect experience in at least one position. Start with your most recent job.

education.title: Add your education
education.text: Recruiters usually check education. Your highest completed level is enough.

editor.schoolPick: Choose the option that best describes your education:
editor.bulletsHint: Each line becomes a bullet point. Start with a verb and show the result, ideally in numbers.
editor.skillsInputPh: Type a skill and press Enter
editor.skillsInputHint: E.g. Excel, customer service, driving licence. 6–12 items work best.
editor.cefrHint: CEFR levels: A1–A2 basic, B1–B2 intermediate, C1–C2 advanced.

ai.summaryHint: AI uses your experience and skills from the CV. Fill those in first for the best result.
ai.privacy: AI requests send only the text of your CV (no contact data or photo). Responses are not stored. Check suggestions before using them.

tailor.title: Tailor to a job offer
tailor.hint: Paste a job ad. AI compares it with your CV like an ATS and a recruiter would.
tailor.score: Match between your CV and this offer. Use the suggestions below to raise it.
tailor.honest: Add only what you really know – interviews check it.

translate.title: Translate the CV
translate.hint: AI translates the whole CV and adapts job titles to the target country. Contact data, dates and layout stay.
translate.undo: Tip: export your CV first to keep both versions. Undo is also available.

tips.consent: Add the GDPR (RODO) consent clause – many employers require it.
tips.photoOptional: A photo is optional; use a professional one if you add it.
tips.photoAvoid: Do not include a photo, date of birth or marital status.
tips.onePage: One page is preferred, especially early in your career.
tips.deLebenslauf: Use a tabular, reverse-chronological Lebenslauf; gaps should be explained.
tips.noPersonal: Leave out personal data unrelated to the job (age, nationality).
tips.usResume: In the US it is called a résumé: short, results-focused, US Letter format.
tips.itConsent: Italian employers often expect a GDPR consent line (Reg. UE 2016/679).
